name: Primary Hypomagnesemia with Hypercalciuria and Nephrocalcinosis with Severe Ocular Involvement
aliases: Hypomagnesemia with Hypercalciuria and Nephrocalcinosis (HHN) Syndrome
Primary Hypomagnesemia with Nephrocalcinosis and Ocular Defects

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic criteria for Primary Hypomagnesemia with Hypercalciuria and Nephrocalcinosis

criteria.description: Persistent hypomagnesemia confirmed by serum magnesium levels below normal reference range
Elevated urinary calcium excretion documented by 24-hour urine collection
Radiological evidence of nephrocalcinosis on renal ultrasound or CT scan
Severe ocular abnormalities including macular coloboma or chorioretinal atrophy
Positive family history consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of hypomagnesemia, hypercalciuria, nephrocalcinosis, and severe ocular involvement
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing for CNNM2 mutations can confirm diagnosis

laboratory: Serum magnesium levels persistently below normal
imaging: Renal ultrasound or CT showing nephrocalcinosis
Ocular imaging revealing macular coloboma or chorioretinal atrophy
genetic: Mutations in CNNM2 gene associated with autosomal recessive inheritance
other: Family history consistent with autosomal recessive pattern

distinguishingFeatures: Less severe or absent ocular involvement
Hypomagnesemia with hypokalemia and metabolic alkalosis

redFlags: Severe ocular malformations leading to vision impairment
Early onset nephrocalcinosis with progressive renal impairment
references: Bockenhauer D, et al. Primary hypomagnesemia with hypercalciuria and nephrocalcinosis: clinical and molecular features. Kidney Int. 2009.
